subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw@2026.7.1-2 root package lacks verifiable build provenance

question: Can a release owner authenticate the original `openclaw@2026.7.1-2` correction build strongly enough to publish a truthful signed attestation for its exact root tarball digest?
rationale: Only the release owner can assess private or expired release artifacts and decide whether a retrospective statement is accurate; repository source alone cannot prove a historical local build recipe or safely authorize a signature.

options.title: Audit and attest if proven
options.body: Review retained correction-build records and publish a signed statement only when they bind the stated source, inputs, and exact npm tarball.

options.title: Record non-attestability
options.body: If the original evidence is insufficient, state that the immutable correction package cannot receive a retrospective provenance claim and rely on the current release path going forward.

recommendation.title: Audit and attest if proven
recommendation.body: Review retained correction-build records and publish a signed statement only when they bind the stated source, inputs, and exact npm tarball.

likelyOwner.reason: The cited correction source commit and reported direct npm publication both connect this release question most closely to `steipete`.
